title: Nobody Hires a Realtor for His Résumé. Here's Mine Anyway.
description: Missoula Realtor and builder Ty Hobbs on football at Montana, five years of teaching, building houses, and how that mix shapes the way he buys and sells real estate.
excerpt: Defensive tackle, high school teacher, home builder, dad of three. Here's how that odd résumé changes the way I work for buyers and sellers in Western Montana.
body_html:
The bottom line

I'm a Missoula Realtor who played defensive tackle at Montana, taught for five years, and now builds a house or two a year. Every one of those jobs changed how I work for buyers and sellers, and here's how.

Most agent bios read like they were written by the same person. Top producer, passion for people, dedicated to your dreams. You've seen it. So instead of that, here's what actually happened.

Spokane kid, Missoula for good

I grew up in Spokane and played tight end at West Valley High School. Montana recruited me, I came over the mountains to play for the Griz, and I never really left. I played defensive tackle at the University of Montana from 2006 to 2010, and my teammates voted me captain in 2010. I've raised my family here ever since. My three kids are Montanans, and none of them had a choice in the matter.

Defensive tackle is not the glamour position. You work in the middle of the mess so someone else gets to make the play. That turns out to be a decent description of a negotiation, too. A lot of my job is absorbing the pressure so my client doesn't have to.

Five years in a classroom

My degree is in secondary education and business marketing, and I taught for five years before I got into real estate. Teaching ruins you for jargon. If a room of people can't follow what you just said, that's on you, not them. Real estate is full of contracts, deadlines, and acronyms that sound like a foreign language to someone buying their first house or selling their last one. I explain them the way I'd explain them to someone I actually want to understand.

Then I started building

Real estate was always the job. The construction came second, and it changed how I look at everything. I build one to two homes a year, and when they're finished they go on the MLS like any other listing. I'm not a custom builder, and I'm a Realtor first. But once you've dealt with framing, inspections, subs who don't show up, and a lot that drains differently than the plans said it would, you can't walk through a house the old way anymore.

Builder's Take

Most people walk into a house and see paint colors, countertops, and staging. I'm looking at the roof, the foundation, and where the water goes when it rains. Paint costs a weekend. A bad foundation costs a different kind of weekend. I'll show you which is which before you write an offer.

Who I like working with

My favorite client is the seller who has to buy again. Two big decisions, tied together, with a timeline that doesn't want to cooperate. That's where straight advice earns its keep. Most of my business comes from past clients and people who know me, and Missoula, Lolo, Frenchtown and Florence are home base. I'll go anywhere in Western Montana for the right deal, including the Bitterroot, the Mission Valley, and Flathead Lake.

The gut-check: would I hire me?

Yes, if you want someone who'll say "don't buy this one" and mean it, who'll tell you the $50,000 kitchen won't pay you back, and who'd rather lose a deal than steer you wrong.

No, if you want a cheerleader who calls every house a dream home. There are plenty of agents for that. I'm probably going to ask you a lot of questions.

What this blog is for

Every week I'll put something here that I'd tell you across a kitchen table: what the Missoula-area market is actually doing, what to look for in a house that most agents miss, honest guides to the places I sell in, and the occasional story. No fluff, no keyword soup. If there's a question you've been afraid to ask a Realtor, text me. It might be next week's post.
